question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{3x+y}{x}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{3x+(vx)}{x} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=3+v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=3 \\ \frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{3}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\mathrm{d}v&=3\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ v&=3\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{x}&=3\ln|x|+C \\ y&=3x\ln|x|+Cx\end{aligned}
$$



The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$.
